Vitamin D deficiency has been found to be more common in children with pediatric celiac disease, according to our data. We have no evidence that this condition leads to a decrease in 25(OH)D levels between normal children and those with CD when adjusted for body mass index.

In the case of Crohn's disease, granulomatous myelotoxicity and enteritis developed in a 21-year-old female within three weeks of initiating sulfasalazine for rheumatoid arthritis. Following a short course of corticosteroids, she had resolution of her cholestatic hepatitis, rash, eosinophilia, and gastrointestinal symptoms with no residual manifestations at seven months follow-up.
